summary: Describes an LDAP extended operation for changing a user's password that does not depend on how the user is identified or how passwords are stored. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: This is a standard way to ask a directory to change your password, no matter how it keeps passwords.

questions: how to change a password over ldap
what is the ldap password modify operation
does ldap password modify need tls
subtitle: An LDAP extended operation for changing a user's password, whatever the identity form or storage.

tldr.problem: Ordinary LDAP update operations change attributes of directory entries, so they cannot change a password when the user has no entry, is not identified by a DN, or the password is not stored as an entry attribute.
tldr.mechanism: A Password Modify extended operation, identified by OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.11.1, carries an optional user identity, old password and new password, and can return a server-generated password.
tldr.outcome: Clients get one way to change passwords independent of identity form and storage, but it provides no protection itself and MUST be used with confidentiality protection such as Start TLS.

facts.label: Advertised in
facts.value: supportedExtension attribute of the root DSE

today: RFC 3062 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on LDAPv3 as defined in RFC 2251.

sections.title: Why Modify Is Not Enough
sections.content:
Traditionally LDAP users were identified by the Distinguished Name of a directory entry, and that entry held a userPassword attribute with one or more passwords. The protocol does not require this. A server may use any suitable attribute, or store passwords outside the directory.

Integration of SASL services that support simple username and password mechanisms (such as DIGEST-MD5) brought in authentication identities that are not LDAP DNs and made password storage the job of the SASL service provider. LDAP update operations act on attributes of an entry, so they cannot change a password when the user has no DN or entry, or when the password is not an attribute of an entry. An alternative mechanism is needed.
sections.eli5: The normal way to edit things in the directory is like editing a card in a card box. If your password is not on a card at all, you need a different way to change it.

sections.title: Request and Response Format
sections.content:
Password Modify is an LDAPv3 Extended Operation identified by the OBJECT IDENTIFIER passwdModifyOID, which is 1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.11.1. The request value is a PasswdModifyRequestValue: a SEQUENCE of three optional octet strings, userIdentity [0], oldPasswd [1] and newPasswd [2]. If a requestValue is provided it SHALL have one or more fields present.

The userIdentity is an octet string form of the user, which may or may not be an LDAPDN. If it is absent, the request acts on the password of the user currently associated with the LDAP session. oldPasswd holds the current password and newPasswd the desired one.

The response is an ExtendedResponse with no responseName. Its optional response value is a PasswdModifyResponseValue holding genPasswd [0], a generated password. If the resultCode is anything other than success (0), the response value MUST be absent.
sections.eli5: The form has three boxes: who you are, your old password and the new one you want. You can leave some empty, and the answer may hold a password the server made up for you.

sections.title: How Servers Must Behave
sections.content:
The server SHALL return success only if it actually changed the password, and otherwise leave the password unmodified and return a non-success resultCode. It SHALL NOT change the password if it does not recognize the provided fields or does not support that combination of fields.

If oldPasswd is present and cannot be verified or is wrong, the server SHALL NOT change the password. If it is absent, the server MAY use other policy to decide.

If the client supplies newPasswd, the server SHALL NOT generate a password. If it does not, the server SHALL either generate one or return a non-success code, and on success it MUST return the generated password in genPasswd. Servers MAY return codes such as unwillingToPerform or confidentialityRequired, and MAY apply administrative policies that restrict the operation.
sections.eli5: The server only says 'done' if it really changed the password. If your old password is wrong, or it does not understand your form, it changes nothing.

sections.title: Advertising and Checking Support
sections.content: Servers SHOULD advertise the operation by listing the OID as a value of the supportedExtension attribute in their root DSE. A server MAY advertise it only when the client is authorized or has set up the needed security protections. Clients SHOULD check that supportedExtension contains the OID before trying the operation.
sections.eli5: Before handing in the form, you check the notice board to see if this office accepts it.

sections.title: Security Requirements
sections.content:
The operation itself gives no integrity or confidentiality. The RFC says it SHOULD NOT be used without adequate security protection and SHALL NOT be used anonymously. Using it without privacy protection is strongly discouraged and may disclose the password to unauthorized parties.

The extension MUST be used with confidentiality protection, such as Start TLS (RFC 2830), and the NULL cipher suite MUST NOT be used. Clients SHOULD NOT submit a request without safeguards in place, and servers SHOULD return a non-success resultCode if protection is insufficient.
sections.eli5: Passwords are secrets, so you must send them through a sealed envelope. The form does not come with one, so you have to bring your own.
